text: Decided to put pgbouncer in transaction pooling mode in front of the orders Postgres cluster; prepared statements must be disabled in the driver because of it.
Pitfall: a Postgres migration that added a column with a volatile default rewrote the whole table and held an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for eleven minutes.
Convention: every Postgres foreign key column gets its own btree index; the planner was doing sequential scans on cascading deletes without them.
Incident: autovacuum fell behind on the events table, transaction ID wraparound warnings appeared, and we ran a manual VACUUM FREEZE overnight.
Runbook: to find blocking queries in Postgres, join pg_stat_activity with pg_locks on pid and look for rows where granted is false.
Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on production Postgres tables; it cannot run inside a transaction block, so that migration file needs the no-transaction flag.
The replica lag alarm on the reporting Postgres instance fires when long analytical queries conflict with WAL replay; max_standby_streaming_delay is now 5 minutes.
Postgres JSONB columns are queried with the @> containment operator, and a GIN index on the column makes those lookups fast.
We raised work_mem only for the nightly aggregation role with ALTER ROLE instead of raising it globally on the Postgres server.
Pitfall: Postgres sequences are not transactional, so gaps in invoice numbers after a rollback are expected, and the auditors were told so.
Runbook for a Postgres major version upgrade: pg_upgrade with --link on a snapshot copy, then ANALYZE every database because planner statistics are not carried over.
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) showed the customer search query reading 40k shared buffers; a partial index on active customers cut it to 200.
Decision: Postgres row-level security isolates tenants, with the tenant id set per transaction through SET LOCAL app.tenant_id.
Incident: the Postgres primary ran out of disk because a replication slot for a dead logical consumer retained all WAL; drop unused slots.
Convention: Postgres timestamp columns are always timestamptz, never timestamp without time zone.
The Postgres server allows 200 connections, so each service instance gets a pool of at most 10 to stay under the limit during deploys.
Postgres statement_timeout is 30 seconds for the web role so a runaway query cannot hold a connection forever.
Pitfall: SELECT FOR UPDATE inside long Postgres transactions queued locks on inventory rows during flash sales; the job queue now uses SKIP LOCKED.
The Postgres audit_log table is partitioned by month with declarative partitioning; old partitions are detached and archived instead of deleted row by row.
pg_stat_statements lists the top Postgres queries by total time each week; the extension has to be in shared_preload_libraries.
Postgres defaults to read committed; the ledger transfer code uses SERIALIZABLE and retries on serialization failures with SQLSTATE 40001.
Runbook: if the Postgres primary fails, promote the synchronous standby with pg_ctl promote and repoint the service DNS record.
A Postgres trigger that updated a counter row on every insert became a lock hotspot; a periodic rollup job replaced it.
Decision: logical replication from the Postgres monolith feeds the search indexer instead of dual writes from the application.
Wide text columns in Postgres were slow to update because of TOAST rewrites; large blobs moved to object storage and only the key stays in the row.
Pitfall: NOT IN with a subquery that can return NULL matches no rows in Postgres; use NOT EXISTS instead.
The Postgres sessions table was 80 percent dead tuples until autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor was lowered for that table.
Convention: avoid Postgres enum types because adding a value needs a migration; use a text column with a check constraint.
The Postgres cluster is backed up with pgBackRest, full weekly and differential daily, and a restore is rehearsed every quarter.
After the instance resize, Postgres shared_buffers went to a quarter of memory and effective_cache_size to three quarters.
Incident: a Postgres advisory lock held by a crashed worker was released only when its connection timed out, which stalled the scheduler for an hour.
Postgres COPY FROM STDIN loads the nightly CSV export ten times faster than batched INSERT statements.
The desktop client opens SQLite in WAL mode so readers do not block the single writer.
Pitfall: SQLite allows one writer at a time; two background tasks writing together got SQLITE_BUSY until busy_timeout was set to 5 seconds.
Convention: every SQLite connection runs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON when it opens, because foreign keys are off by default.
SQLite ALTER TABLE cannot drop a constraint, so our migrations create a new table, copy the rows, drop the old table and rename the new one.
The local cache database runs SQLite with synchronous NORMAL in WAL mode, which survives application crashes but not power loss.
Decision: the schema version of the embedded SQLite store is tracked with PRAGMA user_version instead of a migrations table.
Incident: a SQLite file on a network share was corrupted because file locking is unreliable over SMB; the database must live on a local disk.
An FTS5 virtual table in SQLite indexes the note bodies for search, and the bm25 function ranks the matches.
Runbook: if SQLite reports a malformed database, run PRAGMA integrity_check, then use the .recover command of the sqlite3 shell to rebuild into a new file.
Pitfall: SQLite type affinity accepted a string in an INTEGER column; new tables are declared STRICT.
Wrapping bulk inserts into SQLite in one transaction took 50k rows from two minutes to under a second.
SQLite VACUUM rewrites the whole file and needs free disk equal to the database size, so it runs only when the user asks for it.
The mobile app's SQLite WAL file grew to 1 GB because a long-lived read transaction blocked checkpoints; close cursors promptly.
Convention: SQLite timestamps are stored as integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch, not as text.
rusqlite is built with the bundled feature so every platform ships the same SQLite version.
Decision: the app keeps one SQLite connection per thread rather than sharing one connection behind a mutex.
Pitfall: the SQLite LIKE operator is case-insensitive only for ASCII; Unicode case folding needs a custom collation.
To load a SQLite extension at runtime, enable extension loading on the connection and call load_extension with the entry point name.
SQLite ATTACH DATABASE lets the export command copy tables from the main store into a separate file in one statement.
SQLite page size is fixed when the file is created; change it with PRAGMA page_size followed by VACUUM.
Incident: an app update ran a SQLite migration that held the write lock for 40 seconds on a large profile and froze the UI; migrations now run before the window opens.
The SQLite query planner ignored our index because the column was compared under a different collation; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN showed a full SCAN.
Use INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE for SQLite upserts; INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the row first and breaks foreign keys that point at it.
The integration tests share one in-memory SQLite database across connections through a shared-cache URI.
Convention: primary keys of synced SQLite records are UUID blobs, not INTEGER rowids, so records merge cleanly across devices.
Back up the SQLite store with the online backup API rather than copying the file while it is open.
Pitfall: deleting the -wal and -shm files next to a SQLite database loses committed transactions that were not yet checkpointed.
Deleting 40k ids in one SQLite statement hit the limit on host parameters, so batch deletes are chunked into groups of 500.
ANALYZE fills sqlite_stat1, and PRAGMA optimize when a SQLite connection closes keeps the planner statistics fresh.
Decision: the SQLite busy handler waits up to 5 seconds, then the operation fails with a retryable error shown to the user.
A SQLite generated column extracts the project id from the JSON payload so that it can be indexed.
The SQLite journal_size_limit pragma stops the WAL file from staying large after a big write.
Decision: access tokens are JWTs that expire after 15 minutes; refresh tokens are opaque, stored hashed, and rotated on every use.
Pitfall: the JWT library accepted alg none when no algorithm list was passed, so verification always pins the expected algorithm.
Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite Lax, and the session id is regenerated after login.
Runbook: to revoke a compromised user's sessions, bump their token_version so every outstanding refresh token fails validation.
Passwords are hashed with Argon2id using the security baseline parameters; bcrypt hashes from the old system are upgraded at the next login.
The OAuth login uses the authorization code flow with PKCE; the implicit flow is not allowed for the single-page app.
Incident: clock skew between the auth server and the API rejected fresh tokens as not yet valid; token checks now allow 60 seconds of leeway on nbf and iat.
Convention: the auth middleware returns 401 for a missing or invalid token and 403 when the token is valid but the role lacks permission.
The OAuth state parameter is a random value bound to the browser session to prevent login CSRF.
Decision: service-to-service calls authenticate with mTLS certificates from the internal CA instead of shared API keys.
Token signing keys rotate every 90 days, and the JWKS endpoint publishes both the old and the new key during the overlap.
Pitfall: comparing API key hashes with == leaked timing information; use a constant-time comparison.
The TOTP second factor accepts one step of clock drift and remembers the last used code so it cannot be replayed.
Login rate limiting is per account and per IP address: 10 failures in 15 minutes locks the account for 15 minutes.
Incident: the request logger wrote a refresh token in plain text; authorization headers are now redacted before logging.
The SSO integration maps the identity provider's groups claim to our roles at login, so a change in the IdP takes effect at the next login.
Password reset links carry a single-use token valid for 30 minutes that is invalidated when the password changes.
Convention: permission checks go through authorize(user, action, resource), never ad hoc role string comparisons in handlers.
SAML assertions must be validated for signature, audience and NotOnOrAfter; the library default skipped the audience check.
Decision: customer API keys are shown once at creation and stored only as a SHA-256 hash with a short visible prefix.
OAuth redirect URIs are matched exactly against the registered list after wildcard matching allowed an open redirect.
The permission cache in the auth service has a 60 second TTL, so a revoked permission can linger for up to a minute.
WebAuthn passkeys are offered as a passwordless login, with the credential id and public key stored per device.
Pitfall: logout only deleted the cookie in the browser and the server session stayed valid until server-side invalidation was added.
Support staff impersonation issues a separate token with an act claim, and every action is audited with both user ids.
The CORS policy allows credentials only for our own origins; reflecting any Origin header back was a vulnerability.
Runbook: when the identity provider is down, existing sessions keep working until their refresh, and new logins fail with a status page notice.
An account must verify its email address before it can create API keys.
Tokens carry the tenant id claim and every query checks it against the resource's tenant; one missing check let a tenant read another tenant's invoices.
The CLI logs in with the OAuth device authorization grant: the user types a short code into the browser.
Incident: the Redis session store evicted keys under memory pressure and logged everyone out; sessions now live on a no-eviction instance.
Convention: token signing secrets are read from the vault at startup and never sit in environment files in the repository.
The CI pipeline caches the cargo registry and target directory keyed on the lockfile hash; a cold build takes 14 minutes and a warm one 3.
Pitfall: the release job ran on every tag including pre-releases; the workflow now filters for version tags without a suffix.
Convention: every pull request must pass lint, unit tests and the build on Linux, macOS and Windows before it can merge.
Decision: production deployments happen only from the main branch through the pipeline, never manually from a laptop.
Incident: the CI runner disk filled with Docker layers and every job failed with no space left on device; a nightly prune job now runs on the runners.
Runbook: to rerun a failed deploy, retry only the deploy job; rerunning the whole pipeline rebuilds and publishes a new artifact.
Pipeline build artifacts are kept for 7 days, and release artifacts are copied to long-term storage separately.
Pitfall: secrets are not available to workflows triggered from forks, so the integration job skips with a notice on external pull requests.
The pipeline matrix runs the test suite on the minimum supported toolchain and on the latest stable one.
Decision: third-party CI actions are pinned to a full commit SHA rather than a tag.
Release builds are reproducible: the pipeline sets SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit time and strips build paths.
Incident: the pipeline step that downloads the toolchain failed one run in twenty; it now retries three times with backoff.
Convention: each CI purpose has its own workflow file: build, release and nightly.
Canary deploys go to 5 percent of instances for 30 minutes, and the pipeline promotes them automatically if the error rate stays under the threshold.
The pipeline publishes a container image tagged with the commit SHA and never deploys the latest tag.
Pitfall: the CI cache key ignored the toolchain version, and after an upgrade the restored stale artifacts failed at the link step.
Runbook: to roll back a deploy, run the deploy job with the previous release's image SHA; database migrations only go forward.
The nightly pipeline runs the slow end-to-end suite and posts failures to the team channel.
Decision: the pipeline reports code coverage on pull requests, but coverage does not block a merge.
Pipeline concurrency allows one deploy per environment; a second deploy waits in line instead of running in parallel.
Incident: a debug step in the pipeline echoed a secret into the job log; the logs were purged and the secret rotated.
Self-hosted CI runners execute each job in a fresh container so no state leaks between jobs.
Convention: pipeline steps that need cloud credentials use short-lived OIDC tokens instead of stored keys.
The CI build fails if the lockfile would change, so dependency updates always arrive through a reviewed pull request.
The merge queue runs the full pipeline against the combined result before anything lands on main.
Pitfall: CI path filters skipped the pipeline for a change to the shared build script, and a broken build reached main.
The release pipeline generates release notes from the titles of pull requests merged since the previous tag.
The release pipeline signs the binaries and publishes a checksums file next to them.
Decision: the Windows CI job uses the MSVC toolchain, and Git's link.exe must not shadow the Microsoft linker on the PATH.
The blue-green deploy step switches the load balancer target group only after the new stack passes its health checks.
Incident: two pipelines published the same version number because version bumps were not serialized; the release job now takes a lock.
The pipeline timing dashboard showed dependency installation at 40 percent of total CI time before caching was added.
Pods in the API deployment set CPU and memory requests equal to their limits so they get the Guaranteed QoS class.
Pitfall: the liveness probe queried the database, so a database blip restarted every pod at once; liveness now checks only the process.
Convention: every Kubernetes deployment has a PodDisruptionBudget that allows at most one unavailable replica.
Incident: a node ran out of ephemeral storage because a pod wrote logs into its container filesystem; containers now log to stdout only.
Runbook: if a pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, read kubectl logs --previous for the last crash before restarting anything.
Decision: configuration comes from ConfigMaps mounted as files and secrets from the external secrets operator, never baked into container images.
The horizontal pod autoscaler scales the worker deployment on queue depth through a custom metric instead of CPU.
Container images are built from a distroless base and run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem.
Pitfall: pods were OOMKilled with no application error because the JVM heap was larger than the container memory limit.
Readiness probes fail during startup until caches are warm, so the Service does not route traffic to cold pods.
Convention: every Kubernetes resource carries the app, team and environment labels used by the cost reports.
Incident: a bad NetworkPolicy blocked DNS egress and every pod in the namespace failed to resolve names.
Rolling updates use maxSurge 25 percent and maxUnavailable 0, so cluster capacity never drops during a rollout.
The ingress controller terminates TLS with certificates issued by cert-manager and renewed 30 days before expiry.
Decision: stateful services run outside the cluster on managed databases, and the cluster runs only stateless workloads.
Runbook: to drain a node for maintenance, cordon it, run kubectl drain with --ignore-daemonsets, and wait for the pods to reschedule.
Pitfall: imagePullPolicy Always with a mutable tag ran a different image on each new node.
The cluster autoscaler adds nodes when pods stay pending for more than a minute and removes nodes that are idle for ten.
The Helm charts for all services live in one repository, with the values for each environment in a separate file.
A preStop hook sleeps 10 seconds so the load balancer stops sending traffic before the container receives SIGTERM.
Incident: etcd on the control plane exceeded its space quota and the Kubernetes API server went read-only until compaction ran.
Convention: container resource requests and limits are reviewed monthly against actual usage from the metrics server.
An init container runs the database migration before the application container starts in each pod.
Pod anti-affinity rules spread the replicas across availability zones.
Pitfall: a Kubernetes CronJob with concurrencyPolicy Allow started overlapping runs when one run took longer than the schedule interval.
Decision: the cluster does not run a service mesh; mTLS between pods is handled by the application libraries.
The container entrypoint uses tini as PID 1 so zombie processes are reaped and signals reach the application.
Runbook: to debug a running pod whose image has no shell, attach an ephemeral container with kubectl debug.
Each team gets its own Kubernetes namespace with a resource quota so one team cannot exhaust the cluster.
Incident: the certificate of the internal image registry expired, nodes could not pull, and new pods stayed in ImagePullBackOff.
Terraform manages the cluster and its node pools; manual changes made in the cloud console are overwritten by the next apply.
On SIGTERM the container stops accepting connections and finishes in-flight requests within the pod's 30 second termination grace period.
Decision: server state in the React app lives in the query cache, and only UI state goes into component state.
Pitfall: a useEffect without a dependency array refetched on every render and hammered the API.
Convention: React components are function components with hooks, and no new class components are added.
The bundle analyzer showed the date library at 300 KB, so we switched to a smaller one and lazy-load the locale data.
Incident: a CSS change to a global button class broke the checkout page layout; styles are now scoped with CSS modules.
Forms use controlled inputs with validation on blur, and the submit button moves focus to the first invalid field.
Pitfall: a React list keyed by array index shuffled input values when items were reordered; keys are now stable record ids.
Accessibility: every icon-only button has an aria-label, and keyboard focus shows a visible 2 pixel outline.
Decision: colour and spacing design tokens are CSS custom properties on :root with a dark theme override.
Route-based code splitting keeps the initial JavaScript bundle under 150 KB compressed.
Runbook: when the web app shows a blank page after a deploy, check the browser console for a chunk load error and force a reload.
Wrapping the table rows in React.memo stopped them re-rendering on every keystroke in the filter box.
Pitfall: setting state after a component unmounted produced warnings; the fetch is now cancelled with an AbortController in the effect cleanup.
Convention: the frontend compiles in TypeScript strict mode, and new code never uses any.
Images are served as WebP with width and height attributes so the page layout does not shift while they load.
Incident: a third-party analytics script blocked the browser main thread for 800 ms on mobile; it now loads deferred after first paint.
Global keyboard shortcuts are registered in one React hook and ignored while focus is in a text input.
Decision: the UI formats dates with the Intl API in the user's locale, and the backend always sends ISO 8601 UTC strings.
A virtualised list renders only the visible rows, which made the 10k entry log viewer usable in the browser.
Pitfall: flexbox children overflowed because min-width defaults to auto; min-width 0 fixed the truncated text.
React error boundaries wrap each page so one failing widget does not blank the whole app.
Convention: user-facing strings go through the translation function and are never hard-coded in JSX.
The CSS grid layout of the dashboard page collapses to a single column under 640 pixels wide.
Incident: the service worker cached an old index.html and users saw a stale app for days; HTML now uses a network-first strategy.
The search box debounces input by 250 ms before calling the suggestions endpoint.
Decision: Tailwind utility classes handle layout, and shared React components wrap repeated patterns.
Pitfall: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user content allowed script injection; content is now sanitised before rendering.
Dark mode follows prefers-color-scheme by default, and the user's choice is saved in local storage.
Optimistic updates in the todo list roll back if the server request fails, with a toast explaining the error.
Convention: React component files are named in PascalCase and kept next to their styles and tests.
The Lighthouse performance score dropped after adding a web font, so the font is preloaded with font-display swap.
Modal dialogs trap focus, close on Escape, and return focus to the button that opened them.
Decision: unit tests never touch the network or the real filesystem; integration tests may, inside a temp directory.
Pitfall: a test relied on the iteration order of a hash map and failed at random; it now sorts before asserting.
Convention: test names describe the behaviour, such as rejects_expired_token, not test1.
Incident: a flaky test slept 100 ms to wait for a background job and failed under load; it now polls with a timeout.
Property-based tests generate random inputs for the parser and shrink a failing case to a minimal example.
Snapshot tests of API responses are reviewed like code after blindly updated snapshots hid a regression.
Runbook: to reproduce a flaky test, run it in a loop with the seed printed in the failure message.
Test fixtures come from builder functions with sensible defaults, so each test states only what matters to it.
Pitfall: tests initialised a global logger twice and panicked; initialisation is now guarded by a once cell.
Mutation testing showed the validation tests never checked boundary values, so tests for exactly the limits were added.
Decision: test mocks are used only at process boundaries such as HTTP clients and clocks; internal modules are tested for real.
A fake clock lets the tests advance time to check token expiry without sleeping.
Convention: every bug fix comes with a regression test that fails before the fix.
Incident: tests passed locally but failed on the build server because of the time zone; the test harness now sets TZ to UTC.
Integration tests start the server on port 0 and read back the assigned port so parallel test runs do not collide.
Golden files for the formatter tests live next to the tests, and a flag regenerates them on purpose.
Pitfall: an assertion compared floating point values exactly and failed on another platform; it now uses a tolerance.
Test coverage is a guide, not a target, and nobody adds tests only to raise the number.
Contract tests check that the client and the server agree on the API schema without starting both.
Decision: end-to-end browser tests cover only the five critical user journeys; everything else is tested lower down.
Tests that need a database create a fresh schema for each test and drop it afterwards.
Pitfall: a test left a temp file behind and the next run read stale data; temp directories are now removed on drop.
An hour of fuzzing the decoder found two panics on truncated input, and both inputs became regression tests.
Convention: tests follow arrange, act, assert, with a blank line between the three sections.
The test runner shuffles test order to expose hidden dependencies between tests.
Incident: the test suite took 40 minutes because every test rebuilt the search index; the index is now built once per suite.
Benchmarks run separately from the tests, on a quiet machine, and report the median of several runs.
Decision: a flaky test is fixed or deleted within a week; quarantining it forever is not allowed.
Parameterised tests list each input with its expected output in a table.
Pitfall: the test double returned success for every call, so the error handling path was never exercised.
CLI tests run the real binary with a temporary home directory and check stdout and the exit code.
Every random generator used in tests takes a fixed seed so a failure can be replayed exactly.
Decision: logs are structured JSON with timestamp, level, message, request id and service name on every line.
Pitfall: logging full request bodies at info level filled the disk and leaked personal data; bodies are logged only at debug, redacted.
Convention: metric names carry the service prefix, snake case and the unit, as in request_duration_seconds.
Incident: the high error rate alert did not fire because the metric had no data during the outage; the rule now alerts on absent data too.
Runbook: when a latency alert fires, open the trace of a slow request and find the longest span before checking the hosts.
Distributed tracing propagates the W3C traceparent header through every service call and queue message.
Pitfall: a metric labelled with the user id created millions of time series and overloaded the metrics database.
Alerts page a human only for symptoms users feel, like error rate and latency; causes like high CPU go to a ticket queue.
The API SLO is 99.9 percent of requests under 500 ms over 30 days, with burn rate alerts at 2 and 14 times.
Log levels: error means someone must act, warn means degraded but handled, info is a business event, and debug is for developers.
Incident: the log shipper fell behind and logs arrived 40 minutes late during an outage; it now has its own resource limits.
Every service exposes /metrics for Prometheus scraping alongside its health endpoint.
Decision: trace sampling keeps 10 percent of normal requests and every request that errors or runs slow.
Runbook: to find all logs for one request, search by the request id printed in the error response.
The request duration histogram had no buckets above one second, so buckets at 2, 5 and 10 seconds were added.
Convention: every alert links to a runbook page that says what to check first.
Pitfall: log lines written with several write calls interleaved between threads; each line is now written in one call.
Each service dashboard shows the four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation.
Incident: an alert storm sent 300 pages in ten minutes; alerts are now grouped by service and deduplicated.
Log retention is 14 days for debug and info lines and 90 days for audit events.
Error tracking groups exceptions by stack trace and notifies the owning team when a new issue appears.
Decision: synthetic probes call the login and checkout endpoints every minute from three regions.
Pitfall: counters reset on every deploy; the rate function copes, but the raw graph looked like a traffic drop.
Structured log fields are snake case, and the same field name means the same thing in every service.
On-call handover notes list open incidents, silenced alerts and anything unusual from the shift.
Incident: high-cardinality span attributes made the tracing backend drop data, so attribute values are now bounded.
Convention: a log message is a constant string and the variables go into fields, so logs can be grouped by message.
The queue consumer exports lag per partition, and an alert fires if the lag keeps growing for ten minutes.
Decision: incident postmortems are blameless, written within five days, and list action items with owners.
Runbook: if Prometheus runs out of memory, reduce scrape targets or retention before adding memory.
Exemplars link a latency histogram bucket to a sample trace id so a spike can be drilled into.
Pitfall: the health check endpoint logged every call and produced half of all log volume; successful checks are no longer logged.
Decision: Rust library crates return typed errors with thiserror, and the binary uses anyhow only at the top level.
Pitfall: holding a std Mutex guard across an await point made the future non-Send and blocked the async runtime.
Convention: clippy runs with -D warnings, and pedantic lints are allowed case by case.
Rust functions take &str rather than &String, and impl AsRef<Path> when they accept a path.
Every unsafe block in the Rust code carries a SAFETY comment explaining why its invariants hold.
Pitfall: an integer overflow panicked in a debug build but wrapped silently in release; size arithmetic now uses checked_add.
Decision: tokio is the async runtime everywhere, and runtimes are never mixed in one Rust binary.
Collecting an iterator into a Result stops at the first error, which is how the batch parser fails fast.
Convention: public Rust types derive Debug, and derive Clone only when cloning is cheap or needed.
Incident: a blocking file read inside an async handler stalled every request on that worker thread; it now runs in spawn_blocking.
Returning a reference to a local variable does not compile in Rust; the function returns an owned String instead.
Pitfall: Rc is not Send, so a type containing it cannot cross threads; Arc provides shared ownership across threads.
Cargo features must be additive: enabling a feature may never remove functionality.
Decision: every config and message type derives serde Serialize and Deserialize, and config types use deny_unknown_fields.
The borrow checker rejected mutating a Vec while iterating over it, so the code collects the indices first and mutates afterwards.
Convention: Rust modules are files named after the module rather than mod.rs files.
A Cow<str> return value avoids allocating when the input usually needs no escaping.
Pitfall: a Drop implementation that panicked during unwinding aborted the whole process.
Put #[must_use] on Rust functions whose result is easy to forget, such as builders and guards.
Incident: rustc used 4 GB of memory compiling a huge match generated by a macro; splitting it into functions fixed the build.
Decision: the core crate contains no unsafe code, enforced with forbid(unsafe_code).
Rust trait objects are written with dyn and live behind a pointer such as Box<dyn Trait> or &dyn Trait.
Convention: rustfmt runs with default settings, so formatting is never argued about in review.
Pitfall: f32 does not implement Ord in Rust, so sorting floats needs total_cmp or partial_cmp with a NaN policy.
The Cargo workspace pins every dependency version once in the root manifest, and member crates inherit it.
Send and Sync bounds on the trait let its objects be shared across the multi-threaded tokio runtime.
Rust lazy statics were replaced with std::sync::LazyLock once it became stable.
Pitfall: matching on a non_exhaustive enum from another crate requires a wildcard arm.
Decision: Rust integration tests live in the tests directory and use only the crate's public API.
The newtype pattern wraps ids so a project id cannot be passed where a memory id is expected.
Rust edition 2024 changed which lifetimes impl Trait captures in return position, so check signatures after upgrading.
Convention: Rust error messages start lowercase and do not end with a period.
Decision: the main branch is protected, and changes land through pull requests with one approving review.
Pitfall: a force push to a shared branch erased a colleague's commits; force push only personal branches, and only with --force-with-lease.
Convention: commit messages have an imperative subject line under 72 characters and a body that explains why.
Runbook: to recover a commit lost after a bad reset, find it in git reflog and create a branch at that hash.
Feature branches are rebased onto main before merging so the git history stays linear.
Incident: a large binary was committed and the repository grew by 2 GB; git filter-repo removed it from history and everyone recloned.
Pitfall: the git stash stack is shared by every worktree of a repository, so another session popped my stash.
The .gitattributes file sets text eol=lf for source files so Windows checkouts keep LF line endings.
Decision: git release tags are annotated and signed.
Git worktrees keep a second branch checked out for reviews without stashing anything.
Convention: git branch names start with the author's handle followed by a short topic.
Pitfall: git clean -fdx deleted an ignored local environment file; check the dry run with -n first.
git bisect run with the failing test found the regression in 7 steps across 120 commits.
Small pull requests are squash merged, and larger ones keep their commits when every commit builds.
Incident: a secret was pushed in a commit; rotating it was the real fix, because rewriting git history does not remove it from existing clones.
git blame -w with an ignore-revs file skips whitespace changes and the bulk formatting commit.
Convention: one logical change per commit, so reverting a commit removes exactly one thing.
Runbook: to undo a merged pull request, run git revert -m 1 on the merge commit instead of resetting main.
core.autocrlf is false on the build machines, and .gitattributes alone controls line endings.
Pitfall: a git submodule pointed at a commit that was never pushed, so fresh clones failed to check it out.
Pre-commit hooks run the formatter and the linter, and bypassing them needs a reason in the commit message.
Decision: commits use conventional prefixes such as fix and feat so the changelog can be generated from git log.
